title: Reading and Writing, Years 1 to 3
source_note: Written for the New Zealand Curriculum, Years 1 to 3 (Levels 1 to 2), ages 5 to 8. Covers letter sounds, blends and digraphs, rhyming, sight words, simple punctuation, singular and plural, opposites and alphabetical order. Checked 2026-08-30.

questions.prompt: Which letter makes the first sound in 'sun'?
questions.explanation: The word 'sun' starts with the S sound, like 'sss'.

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'cat'?
questions.explanation: 'Cat' and 'hat' both end in the 'at' sound, so they rhyme.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of 'big'?
questions.explanation: 'Small' means the opposite of 'big': not much size at all.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of 'hot'?
questions.explanation: 'Cold' is the opposite of 'hot'. Think of ice instead of fire.

questions.prompt: One dog, two ___?
questions.explanation: Most words just add 's' to show more than one, so two dogs, not one dog.

questions.prompt: Which letter makes the first sound in 'moon'?
questions.explanation: 'Moon' starts with the M sound, like 'mmm'.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of 'up'?
questions.explanation: 'Down' is the opposite of 'up': one goes higher, the other goes lower.

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'dog'?
questions.explanation: 'Dog' and 'frog' both end in the 'og' sound, so they rhyme.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the 'sh' sound?
questions.explanation: 'Ship' starts with 'sh', like a quiet 'shhh'.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the 'ch' sound?
questions.explanation: 'Chin' starts with 'ch', like the sound at the start of 'chip'.

questions.prompt: Which word starts with the 'th' sound?
questions.explanation: 'Thumb' starts with 'th', made by putting your tongue near your teeth.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelled the right way?
questions.explanation: 'Said' is the correct spelling, even though it does not sound the way it looks.

questions.prompt: One box, two ___?
questions.explanation: Words ending in 'x' add 'es' to show more than one, so two boxes.

questions.prompt: Which mark ends a question?
questions.explanation: A question mark shows a sentence is asking something, like 'Are you ready?'

questions.prompt: Which mark ends most sentences?
questions.explanation: A full stop shows a sentence has finished telling you something.

questions.prompt: Which word should start with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: Days of the week, like Monday, always start with a capital letter.

questions.prompt: Which letter comes first in the alphabet?
questions.explanation: A is the very first letter of the alphabet, before B, C and D.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of 'day'?
questions.explanation: 'Night' is the opposite of 'day': one is light, the other is dark.

questions.prompt: Which word ends with the 'sh' sound?
questions.explanation: 'Fish' ends with 'sh', like the sound for 'be quiet'.

questions.prompt: Which word ends with the 'ch' sound?
questions.explanation: 'Lunch' ends with 'ch', the same sound as the start of 'chip'.

questions.prompt: Which word ends with the 'th' sound?
questions.explanation: 'Bath' ends with 'th', made with your tongue between your teeth.

questions.prompt: One mouse, two ___?
questions.explanation: 'Mouse' changes to 'mice' for more than one, it does not just add 's'.

questions.prompt: One child, two ___?
questions.explanation: 'Child' changes to 'children' for more than one, an unusual plural to remember.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of 'empty'?
questions.explanation: 'Full' is the opposite of 'empty': one has nothing in it, the other has everything it can hold.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of 'wet'?
questions.explanation: 'Dry' is the opposite of 'wet': no water on it at all.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: 'Because' has an 'au' in the middle, easy to forget when you sound it out.

questions.prompt: Which word comes first in alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: 'Apple' starts with A, the earliest letter here in the alphabet.

questions.prompt: A sentence that asks something ends with a ___?
questions.explanation: Asking sentences end with a question mark, not a full stop.

questions.prompt: One foot, two ___?
questions.explanation: 'Foot' changes to 'feet' for more than one, it does not add 's'.

questions.prompt: One tooth, two ___?
questions.explanation: 'Tooth' changes to 'teeth' for more than one, just like foot changes to feet.

questions.prompt: One man, two ___?
questions.explanation: 'Man' changes to 'men' for more than one, an unusual plural worth remembering.

questions.prompt: Which comes first in alphabetical order: monkey, moon, mouse?
questions.explanation: All three start with 'mo', so look at the next letter: 'monkey' has 'n', which comes before 'o' and 'u'.

questions.prompt: Which word always starts with a capital letter?
questions.explanation: The word 'I', meaning yourself, is always written with a capital letter.

questions.prompt: Which word already means more than one, without adding 's'?
questions.explanation: 'Children' already means more than one child, unlike 'cats' which just adds 's'.

questions.prompt: 'Sam ran to the shop.' Which mark ends this sentence?
questions.explanation: This sentence just tells you something happened, so it ends with a full stop, not an exclamation mark.

questions.prompt: Which comes first in alphabetical order: cat, car, cap?
questions.explanation: All three start with 'ca', so look at the next letter: 'cap' has 'p', which comes before 'r' and 't'.

questions.prompt: Which comes first in alphabetical order: plum, plan, place, plate?
questions.explanation: All start with 'pl', so compare further: 'place' has 'c' next, which comes before 'n' in 'plan' and 't' in 'plate'.

questions.prompt: One person, two ___?
questions.explanation: 'Person' changes to 'people' for more than one, a tricky plural that does not follow the usual rule.

questions.prompt: Which word rhymes with 'chair', even though it looks different?
questions.explanation: 'Chair' and 'bear' sound the same at the end, even though they are spelled differently.

questions.prompt: Which sentence needs a question mark at the end?
questions.explanation: 'Where is the cat' is asking something, so it needs a question mark, not a full stop.
